name: Mass estimator: fresh operating-range assessment

aims: Validate on fresh draws the archive-derived contrasts between relative estimator advantage and absolute accuracy, without tuning a point rule or selecting a global winner.
Map cell-specific performance over effective force and acceleration SNR, retaining both channel orientations and same-law point summaries.
Assess stated accuracy benchmarks and their simultaneous Monte Carlo uncertainty; benchmarks are not application requirements supplied by the user.
data_generating_mechanisms: Newton II is assumed correct. One compatible latent 3D pair has true force=[F,0,0], true acceleration=[A,0,0], positive physical mass F/A. Common direction is used only by the simulator and remains unknown to inference.
Independently cross effective force and acceleration SNR values [1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16] for 64 cells, using known independent isotropic Gaussian coordinate SD 1 in both channels.

Simulate one effective reading per channel. This is also the sufficient-mean experiment for independent stable repeated Gaussian readings with known SDs after standardization; no extra effective sample size is claimed. Held-out predictions belong to the configured effective-reading experiment and are secondary, not a recreation of earlier raw-reading prediction tasks.

Use R=10000 independent replicates per cell, with a fresh training seed and independent held-out seed. The same replicate-index noise is shared across cells to aid comparisons; cells cannot be pooled as independent evidence.

The grid excludes true-null and subunit effective SNR, whose nonidentification and weak-signal limits were already analyzed. It is a focused positive-signal assessment, not robustness to unknown calibration, correlation, non-Gaussian noise or varying excitation.
estimands: Fixed true mass F/A separately for each truth cell. Changing one channel SNR with the other fixed also changes physical mass. Constant-ratio rays distinguish changing signal strength at fixed mass.
Probability of a positive mass estimate lying in [m/K,K*m], including all attempted trials, for fixed factors K=1.25,1.5,2. Report success and failure, not only a method ranking.
Repeated-experiment mean capped squared log loss with cap factor 2, and paired flat-minus-comparator differences in each cell.

Reference absolute-accuracy benchmarks are at least 90% and at least 95% success for each K. Classify each cell as supported, below_target or unresolved using simultaneous Monte Carlo bounds; passing the benchmark is not a claim of application adequacy.
Conditional mass-law coverage, interval width and both miss directions are retained secondary outputs; point accuracy does not validate conditional intervals.
methods: Use the existing isotropic comparison engine unchanged, retaining every implemented method and the existing quadrature refinement checks.

Primary interpretation compares flat_joint E[f]/E[alpha], flat_median, flat_geometric and norm_ratio; norm_floor and positive_profile remain secondary comparators. Same-law alternatives distinguish benefits shared by the conditional law from the particular readout.

Predeclared follow-up contrasts: flat-minus-norm failure at factor 1.5 is expected negative at effective (F,A)=(1,4) and positive at (4,4), based on earlier archived observations. Both are reevaluated with new noise.

Every invalid/nonpositive/nonfinite output is retained as a tolerance failure and maximum capped loss. No law-rejection gate, output clipping, failed-trial deletion, adaptive stopping or parameter tuning is introduced.
performance_measures: Use paired method differences on identical replicate IDs. Pointwise MCSE is the sample SD of the paired difference divided by sqrt(R), separate from numerical refinement error.

Freeze a single 95% simultaneous DKW family over all archived point methods in all 64 cells. For the expected 11 methods L=704 marginal error CDFs; use the actual saved method inventory and epsilon=sqrt(log(2*L/.05)/(2*R)).

Absolute success bands are empirical success plus/minus epsilon, clipped to [0,1]. A target is supported if the lower bound reaches it, below_target if the upper bound is below it, otherwise unresolved. The event covers all error thresholds and both target levels without an additional multiplicity factor.

Paired survival-difference bands have halfwidth 2*epsilon. Normalized capped squared-log loss is an integral of survival with positive weights summing to 1, so the same family event covers these risk differences. Raw cap-2 loss bounds multiply by log(2)^2.

At R=10000 and L=704, marginal epsilon is about .02263 and difference halfwidth about .04527. These deliberately conservative bounds may leave near-target cells unresolved; zero observed failures never implies zero risk.

Registry precision fields retain the runner's existing factor-two/cap-two/coverage metrics. The broader factor-1.25/1.5/2 accuracy ladder and simultaneous rules above are frozen scientific analysis choices and are computed from the saved outputs.

Report only sampled cells. Do not infer a continuous boundary, monotonic accuracy beyond a cut, an observed-data acceptance rule, or an overall average over arbitrary cells. Performance uncertainty here is Monte Carlo error for the fixed implemented methods, excluding quadrature bias and model misspecification.

methodology.title: Morris, White and Crowther: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
Gneiting: Making and Evaluating Point Forecasts
Reeve: A short proof of the Dvoretzky-Kiefer-Wolfowitz-Massart inequality

interpretation: Designed after exploratory archived-data sensitivity analysis at .tools/loss_sensitivity_20260921/main-reviewed/analysis.json. Fresh observations supply a follow-up, not a claim that the grid was chosen without earlier evidence.
Carried-forward managed context is the coherent snapshot used by the investigation; this protocol does not refresh, reorganize or alter managed sources.
Benchmark thresholds are explicit reference levels. An application-specific target and its observed-data assessment remain open.
All 64 cells, all implemented methods and all failures remain visible. The same simultaneous family covers selected subsets; no winner count is a scientific endpoint.

Accuracy in weak balanced-signal cells can reflect shrinkage toward the noise-ratio mass scale 1. Do not treat accuracy at that selected mass as identification or apply a true-SNR map as an observed-data acceptance rule.
Keep the fixed R even if an interim cell looks decisive or inconclusive. Resume interrupted experiments under the unchanged source/configuration contract.
